sections.h2: What is Simpson County, Kentucky, and where does Franklin fit?
sections.html:
Simpson County sits on Kentucky's southern edge in the Pennyroyal Plateau region, right against the Tennessee line. Allen, Logan and Warren counties gave up land to form it in 1819, and it honors Captain John Simpson, a militia officer killed at the Battle of River Raisin in 1812. Warren County borders it on the north, Allen on the east, Logan on the west, and Sumner and Robertson counties in Tennessee on the south.

Of its 236 square miles, 234 are land. Franklin is its lone city and its seat of government. Franklin received its charter from the state assembly on November 2, 1820, on a 62 acre tract bought from William Hudspeth, and carries the name of Benjamin Franklin. The 2020 census counted 10,176 people in Franklin and 19,594 in the county, so roughly half the county lives in town and the rest in farm and small community settings.

sections.h2: How do Simpson County home values and incomes compare in the Census data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 20,788 residents for July 2025, up from 19,595 at the 2020 base, in 9,172 housing units and 8,025 households of about 2.44 people.

  • Households living in a home they own, 2020 to 2024: 66.7 percent.
  • Median value of owned homes: $229,400.
  • Monthly owner cost: $1,299 with a mortgage, $480 without.
  • Median rent: $1,012.
  • Median household income: $59,858, with 14.6 percent of residents under the poverty line and 18.8 percent of adults holding a four year degree.

Owners hold two thirds of the occupied homes, so most sales here involve a house that has had a long-term resident rather than a landlord.

sections.h2: What should a house seller know about Franklin?
sections.html:
Franklin's history includes a 1948 plane crash that sent a Kentucky Air National Guard pilot to his death while chasing an unidentified object, commemorated by a roadside historical marker at the tourism office, and the 1968 wedding of Johnny Cash and June Carter at Franklin First United Methodist Church. Kentucky Downs, a racetrack on the state border, hosts the Kentucky Cup Turf Festival.

  • Simpson County Schools runs Franklin, Lincoln and Simpson elementary schools, Franklin-Simpson Middle School, Franklin-Simpson High School and an alternative West Campus.
  • Franklin Mennonite Elementary and Faith Baptist Academy are private options, and Goodnight Memorial Library serves the town.
  • The city's Franklin Forward comprehensive plan covers land use, housing and community facilities, and the zoning map is posted on the city site.
  • Yearly precipitation averages about 50.5 inches, with only 4.3 inches of it as snow.

sections.h2: How does the Simpson County PVA value property?
sections.html: The Property Valuation Administrator puts every parcel on the roll at fair cash value, using January 1 as the date, as Section 172 of the Kentucky Constitution requires. Setting rates and taking payments belong to other offices. The January 1 rule matters at a sale, because a buyer who closes later in the year may never see the bill. The PVA says to phone the Sheriff at 270-586-7425 if one does not arrive, and the PVA itself answers at 270-586-4261 on weekdays from 8 to 4.

sections.h2: Who sends and collects Simpson County property tax bills?
sections.html:
Three offices share the job. The County Clerk prepares and prints the bills and records deeds, the Sheriff collects the county and school portions, and the City of Franklin runs its own tax office at 117 W Cedar for city bills. Franklin's commission sets the city rates using a state formula, and the city office treats a postmark as proof of on-time payment.

City bills follow the deed records in the clerk's office on January 1. When a property sold afterward, the previous owner remains the city taxpayer, and the city office gives original bills only to the addressee. An escrow company that wants an electronic copy of the billing register pays $100, while substitute bills and master payment lists are taken at no charge.

sections.h2: What are the Simpson County payment deadlines and penalties?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 supplies the schedule. A bill settled in full by November 1 earns 2 percent off. The printed amount carries no penalty through December 31, January adds 5 percent, and 10 percent applies after January ends. The city says its own issue, penalty and delinquent dates vary each year, so read the dates printed on each bill.

Anyone with an interest in the property, such as a tenant or a lender, may pay a delinquent bill without the owner's permission if the Sheriff is shown proof, and a payer can ask to be treated as a transferee (KRS 134.119). After the Sheriff files unpaid claims with the County Clerk, the clerk holds them as certificates of delinquency.

sections.h2: How does a Simpson County owner appeal an assessment?
sections.html:
An appeal begins with a conference at the PVA's office. KRS 133.045 keeps the real property roll open for inspection through 13 days from early May, six days a week, and the conference must be requested before that period closes. The 2026 period is over. Under the state process, an owner who still disagrees files with the County Clerk, and three local residents hear the case informally, with no attorney required.

The Franklin city site describes the local assessment board as a body with three year terms that meets once a year, with seats filled by the city, the Fiscal Court and the county judge. Bring comparable sales, a recent appraisal or photos of damage. A losing owner can carry the case to the state's tax appeals board.

sections.h2: Which Simpson County and Franklin rules can hold up a house sale?
sections.html:
Franklin applies the International Property Maintenance Code through its Code Enforcement department, which takes yard sale permits and public nuisance complaints through its citizen portal. The Planning and Zoning Commission follows KRS Chapter 100 and its own comprehensive plan, and its staff can be reached at 270-596-2756. The city also keeps a lienholder notification process listed among its services.

A home with a nuisance complaint, an unpaid city tax bill or a permit left open is harder to close. Ask city staff about open cases at an address before you list, and confirm county and city tax payoffs separately.

sections.h2: What does a Simpson County seller owe at closing?
sections.html:
Kentucky's deed transfer tax falls on the seller: 50 cents on each $500 of price, taken by the County Clerk at the recording counter (KRS 142.050). A sale at the county's typical $229,400 value owes $229.50. Add prorated property tax, any lien payoff and agent fees if you list. Owners who qualify for the homestead or disability exemption should confirm with the PVA that it is on file before the sale, since the PVA administers both. A cash offer avoids agent fees and repair demands, which can matter for an older farmhouse or a rental needing work, but the net after payoffs is the number to compare.

faqs.q: Does Franklin bill its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Franklin sets rates through its commission and runs a tax office at 117 W Cedar, open weekdays until 4 p.m. Central time. Houses inside city limits get two bills, one from the county and one from the city.

faqs.q: Who is billed if I buy a Simpson County house after January 1?
faqs.a: The former owner is the taxpayer of record for that year. The PVA mails the bill to the new owner when it can, and a buyer who receives nothing can call the Sheriff at 270-586-7425.

faqs.q: When does the Simpson County early payment discount end?
faqs.a: On November 1. Full payment by then takes 2 percent off, and the face amount holds through December 31 under KRS 134.015. Penalties of 5 and then 10 percent follow.

faqs.q: Where is a Simpson County assessment appeal filed?
faqs.a: After a PVA conference, file with the County Clerk at 105 E Kentucky St. The conference has to happen while the roll is open for inspection, which starts in early May.

faqs.q: What deed tax comes out of a Simpson County sale?
faqs.a: Half a dollar per $500 of price, with a partial block counted whole, so a $229,400 sale owes $229.50 through the County Clerk at recording.
